candidates.title: Mobility infrastructure encodes housing pressure
candidates.shift: An artist-built device slows shared bikes in NYC blocks under high housing pressure, making an invisible economic condition physically legible through everyday mobility infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if mobility hardware can be tuned to socioeconomic data, it could foreshadow dynamic-access or dynamic-speed infrastructure tied to neighborhood economics — unsettling for property and mobility operators alike.
candidates.evidence: Justin Blinder's 'Ground Truth' project physically slows Citi Bikes using housing-pressure data layered onto bike-share hardware in NYC.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of civic/artistic hacking of shared mobility infrastructure to expose socioeconomic data. If normalized, it could presage infrastructure that responds dynamically to neighborhood economic indicators, reshaping how access is allocated near retail and housing.
candidates.author: Ellen Eberhardt

candidates.title: Underground construction as heritage-site expansion strategy
candidates.shift: A national museum is expanding via a 1,300m² underground extension rather than surface building, suggesting underground construction as a growing response to space-constrained heritage sites.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as urban land grows scarcer and heritage protections tighten, going underground may become a standard construction strategy for retail/civic expansion in dense historic cores.
candidates.evidence: AART wins the competition for an underground Royal Treasury extension at Rosenborg Castle, Copenhagen, with landscape and structural partners.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from surface expansion to underground construction in heritage-constrained sites, driven by land scarcity and preservation rules. If generalized, could inform how constrained urban retail/civic sites expand without growing surface footprint.
candidates.author: Reyyan Dogan

candidates.title: Compute-as-loyalty-currency bundled into retail transactions
candidates.shift: Chinese businesses are bundling free AI tokens/compute credits with coffee purchases, credit cards, and food orders, turning compute access into a retail loyalty and payment perk.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an early instance of 'compute' becoming a retail loyalty currency the way points or cashback are today — directly relevant to the open compute hunt zone; could migrate west via checkout/loyalty mechanics.
candidates.evidence: Rest of World reports five ways compute power (AI tokens) is bundled into consumer retail products like coffee, credit cards, and telco plans in China.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from compute as backend infrastructure to compute as a bundled consumer perk/loyalty currency, driven by AI token oversupply and consumer AI push in China. If it spreads, retailers may need to manage 'compute inventory' like a loyalty asset.
candidates.author: Kinling Lo

candidates.title: Building-scale energy flexibility becoming grid-critical infrastructure
candidates.shift: New Zealand case studies show building automation platforms and virtual power plants integrating rooftop solar, batteries and flexible loads to manage distribution-grid voltage stability, pushing building energy management from optional to grid-essential.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as DER penetration rises, individual buildings (including retail stores) may need to become active grid participants (VPP nodes) rather than passive energy consumers — a new 'energy asset' category for real estate.
candidates.evidence: Two Aotearoa NZ studies detail residential building automation for solar/flexible-load integration and PowerFactory-Python co-simulation of VPP voltage stability under high DER penetration.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from buildings as passive energy consumers to buildings as active grid-balancing assets, driven by DER penetration and decarbonization goals. If scaled, retail real estate may need onsite battery/solar-VPP contracts to manage costs and grid compliance.
candidates.author: Admire Muravu, Alan C. Brent

candidates.title: Carbon-negative wall material made from forestry waste
candidates.shift: A Finnish company has launched MO6, a wall-surfacing material made almost entirely of carbon from forestry offcuts, marketed as the world's most carbon-storing building material.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: signals a new construction-materials category — carbon-storage-as-feature — that could require new certification/labeling standards, an absence in current material specification systems.
candidates.evidence: Elementic (Finland) unveiled MO6, thick lightweight tiles made from forestry-industry offcuts, described as almost pure carbon.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from carbon-neutral to carbon-storing building materials, driven by circular forestry byproducts and climate construction targets. If adopted broadly, could create new procurement categories and certifications for retail fit-out materials.
candidates.author: Nat Barker

candidates.title: Non-penetrating structural systems for rooftop retrofits
candidates.shift: A UK construction-systems manufacturer's integrated rail system lets rooftop terraces support planting, seating and entertainment without penetrating the waterproofing membrane.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as retailers/landlords convert underused rooftops into amenity or micro-fulfillment space, non-invasive retrofit systems could become an enabling category — an absence being standardized rooftop retrofit-without-penetration methods.
candidates.evidence: Ryno's TerraSmart Lattice Rail System integrates planting, balustrading and seating on a London rooftop terrace without penetrating waterproofing, per Dezeen.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from invasive rooftop construction to modular, non-penetrating retrofit systems, driven by demand for adaptive reuse of existing rooftops. If it spreads, could unlock underused retail rooftop real estate for amenity or logistics use.
candidates.author: Dezeen staff

candidates.title: Road design as economic-leakage determinant
candidates.shift: A new database quantifies how road design determines whether local travel spending stays in a community or leaks out, tying infrastructure form directly to local economic retention.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: reframes road/parking infrastructure as a direct economic-value lever for surrounding retail — could inform site selection and municipal infrastructure negotiations differently than traffic-volume metrics alone.
candidates.evidence: Strong Towns cites a new database correlating road design typologies with local economic retention/leakage patterns.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from traffic-flow-centric road evaluation to economic-retention-centric evaluation, driven by new data tools measuring local spending. If adopted by planners, could reshape how retail site selection and municipal capital investment are justified.

candidates.title: Green-space preservation colliding with affordable-housing land supply
candidates.shift: US West Coast cities are running out of land that satisfies both affordable-housing mandates and green-space expectations, turning a housing crisis into an explicit land-value tradeoff.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: the same land-value tension applies to retail real estate near green amenities — could foreshadow zoning fights over converting retail parking/parcels into either housing or green space, squeezing store footprints.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily analysis of West Coast cities (LA to Seattle) facing parcel scarcity balancing affordable-housing commitments against green-space values.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from land questions framed purely as housing supply to explicit values tradeoffs between green space and housing, driven by parcel scarcity. If it intensifies, could pressure surface parking lots and low-density retail sites as conversion targets.
candidates.author: Ankitha Gattupalli

candidates.title: Loyalty programs as unmanaged financial liability
candidates.shift: Petco's overly generous loyalty program cost the company millions, revealing that loyalty programs function as unhedged financial liabilities rather than pure marketing tools.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: loyalty programs may need actuarial/insurance-style risk modeling — an absence, since no standard 'loyalty liability' financial product/category yet exists as retailers scale point-based generosity.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive reports Petco Perks' overly generous rewards structure caused millions of dollars in losses.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a marketing tool (loyalty program) behaving like an unmanaged financial liability, driven by competitive pressure to over-reward. If repeated across retailers, could spur demand for loyalty-liability insurance or actuarial modeling tools.
candidates.author: Bryan Wassel

candidates.title: Battlefield drone data becoming a tradeable commercial asset
candidates.shift: Data generated by drones in Ukraine's war is spawning a new, unregulated marketplace expected to outlast the conflict, creating a novel data-asset class tied to physical sensing infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, off-map: if drone-sensing data becomes a commercial asset class, it could eventually feed into retail/urban surveillance, delivery-drone insurance, and site-monitoring data markets — touching Tech/Infrastructure branches later.
candidates.evidence: MIT Technology Review reports a 'Wild West' marketplace forming around drone data from the Ukraine war, expected to persist beyond the conflict.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from drone data as military byproduct to drone data as tradeable commercial asset, driven by wartime sensor proliferation. If commercialized, could seed data-market infrastructure later relevant to commercial drone delivery, insurance and site-security data.
candidates.author: Cory Alpert
